title: "Part 1 – Credibility and tools"
---
::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
**Slides.** [Open the deck at this part](../../slides/cohabitation-one-day.html#/part-1-credibility-and-tools){target="_blank"} in its own tab, or follow it on the [slides page](slides.qmd).
:::

Part 1 asks what a claim in social science is for, why people describe the field as being in crisis, how three very large studies measured the problem, and what a computational toolchain has to do with any of it. The hands-on work comes at the end and runs into the first break, so that if your machine gives trouble you miss none of the talk.

| Work through | What you do | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| Slides, the opening | The plan of the day, the two kinds of aim, what you will understand and what you will be able to do, and what you do not need: no git, and no GitHub or OSF account. | 6 minutes |
| Slides, Part 1 | Follow the talk: what social science is for; false positives and forking paths; the evidence from replications and many-analysts studies; incentives and questionable research practices, which matter far more than fraud; the red-card study, in which twenty-nine teams analysed one dataset, and the estimates they returned; why 'replication' names three different operations, set out as a matrix of data against analysis, with a quick check on it; and the practices of open research. | 24 minutes |
| Slides, SCORE and Multi100 | The SCORE programme and its three studies, of reproducibility, robustness and replicability, with the results of each and the finding that the three do not travel together. Then Multi100 from the position of an analyst inside it: what an analyst received, the two tasks, and how the results were put on a common scale. | 28 minutes |
| Slides, the tools segment | Open-source software, the toolchain, plain-text file formats and what happens when you render, where data and code are archived, the workspace and the browser lab, and what the tools cannot do. An optional run of five slides covers programming languages, editors, packages, version control and licences. Note anything that you might switch to. | 18 minutes |
| Your workspace, or [Browser lab](../../cases/cohabitation/lab.qmd#task-1-setup) Task 1 | Task 1, the setup check. Open the workspace folder in your IDE and run `source("R/check_setup.R")` until every line prints OK; the last check fits the reference specification and prints −0.730 on the log scale, a number that you meet again later. Everything else that the day needs, the file of Task 3 included, is already in the `data/` folder of the workspace. In the browser lab, wait for the R engine, run the setup cell and check that it reports 19,183 cohabitations; the warm-up on the three Rs gives you something to do while the engine downloads. | 14 minutes, and the 30-minute break after it if you need more |

**By the end of the part** you have R running with the 19,183 first cohabitations of the course data loaded, and you can tell apart the three operations that go under the single word 'replication'.
